title: Inclinations as persuasive arguments; variety and use; occasion can also serve as argument
pass_a_gloss: X. Inclinations toward believing are arguments by which unbelievers are moved and induced that they acknowledge the Christian religion credible and more probable than all others by human persuasion; in the same sense they are elsewhere called motives. XI. But their variety and use is to be considered. Often it happens that an occasion is not only in the place of an occasion but also of an argument by which we are moved to assenting. Thus the Church proposing the scriptures not only furnishes an occasion but also moves as an argument when I consider so many nations by unanimous consent embracing the scriptures as divinely revealed. The same reason is of miracles and of martyrs: A religion which is confirmed by miracles and for which men meet death cannot be empty.
pass_b_english: X. Inclinations toward believing are arguments by which unbelievers are moved to acknowledge the Christian religion as credible and, by human persuasion, more probable than all others. Elsewhere they are called motives.

XI. Their variety and use must be considered. Often an occasion is not only in the place of an occasion but also of an argument. So the Church, proposing the Scriptures, moves as an argument when I consider so many cultivated nations embracing them with one consent as divinely revealed. The same holds for miracles and martyrdoms: A religion confirmed by miracles, and for which people face death, cannot be empty.
source_text:
X. Inclinationes ad credendum sunt argumenta, quibus infideles moventur… ut religionem Christianam credibilem… agnoscant; alias motivae dicuntur.

XI. Consideranda earum varietas & usus. Saepe occasio non tantum est loco occasionis, sed & argumenti… Religio quae miraculis confirmatur & pro qua homines mortem oppetunt non potest esse vana.
